title: Gravitational Potential Energy of a System
short: ΔU = mgΔh belongs to the Earth–object system, and only changes in it matter.
trouble: Students think the potential energy depends on the path taken between two heights.

blocks.html: In Gravitational Potential Energy you met $PE = mgh$. Now look closely at where that energy lives. It isn't stored in the lifted book alone; it belongs to the book and Earth together, because it depends on how far apart they are.

For an object–Earth system near Earth's surface, $\role[change in gravitational potential energy]{energy}{\Delta U_g} = \role{mass}{m}\role[acceleration of gravity]{acceleration}{g}\,\role[change in height]{position}{\Delta h}$. Only changes in $U_g$ matter, so you may put $U_g = 0$ at any convenient height. $\Delta U_g$ depends only on the change in height, not on the path.

Lift a book at steady speed and you do work $mg\,\Delta h$ against gravity, but the book's kinetic energy doesn't change. The energy went into the separation between the book and Earth. Gravity's work on any path depends only on how far up or down you end, because only the vertical parts of the path count. So the stored energy is path-independent, and that is what makes it a potential energy.

blocks.name: ph-energy

opts.task: Watch the gravitational energy bar. It depends only on the cart's height, whatever the shape of the track.

blocks.cap: A cart on a hilly track: Ug rises and falls with height alone.

blocks.title: Up the stairs
blocks.q: A $55\ \text{kg}$ student climbs to a floor $3.5\ \text{m}$ higher. Find $\Delta U_g$ for the student–Earth system.

blocks.title: Path does not matter
blocks.q: A $20\ \text{kg}$ cart is pushed up a winding ramp $30\ \text{m}$ long to a platform $4\ \text{m}$ higher. Find $\Delta U_g$.
steps: Only the change in height counts: $\Delta U_g = (20)(9.8)(4) = 784\ \text{J}$.
The $30\ \text{m}$ ramp length is a distractor.

blocks.title: Choosing the zero
blocks.q: A $2\ \text{kg}$ box on a shelf $1.8\ \text{m}$ above the floor, next to a $0.8\ \text{m}$ table. Find $U_g$ with $U_g = 0$ at the floor, then at the tabletop.
steps: Different values, but moving the box from the shelf to the floor changes $U_g$ by $-35.3\ \text{J}$ in both choices.

blocks.html: Thinking the potential energy depends on the path taken between two heights: that a long gentle ramp stores more energy than a short steep one. The ramp takes a smaller force over a longer distance, and the work against gravity comes out the same. Check: $\Delta U_g$ has only $\Delta h$ in it, never a path length.
